overview: The paper proposes ∂lift (DiffLift), a general differentiable framework that learns to lift input graphs into higher-order topological domains (hypergraphs, cell complexes, simplicial complexes) in an end-to-end fashion, using node embeddings to parameterize candidate cells and probabilistically accepting them via straight-through estimators to boost Topological Neural Network performance.

modules.name: Configuration Management
modules.description: Parses and manages global experimental settings, including dataset specifications, target topological domain types, GNN backbone configurations, maximum domain dimensions, and training hyperparameters.

modules.name: Data Loading and Preprocessing
modules.description: Loads graph and node classification benchmark datasets, applies data cleaning, converts formats for compatibility with topological libraries, and implements dataset splitting strategies (random vs. public splits).

modules.name: Node Embedding Generator
modules.description: Implements the upstream graph neural network backbones (e.g., GIN, GPS) responsible for computing latent vertex-level representations from the input graph's structure and features.

modules.name: Candidate Cell Elicitation
modules.description: Implements the iterative, domain-specific logic for generating candidate higher-order cells, such as identifying k-nearest neighbors in the embedding space for dimension 1, and extracting cycle bases or cliques for dimensions 2 and above.

modules.name: Cell Acceptance Probability Estimator
modules.description: Constructs the neural networks (MLPs, DeepSets) that map candidate cell embeddings to acceptance probabilities, and implements the Bernoulli sampling mechanism integrated with the Straight-Through Estimator for differentiable discrete decisions.

modules.name: Adaptive Hyperedge Size Sampler
modules.description: Implements the mechanism for dynamically determining the size of candidate hyperedges by sampling from a categorical distribution parameterized by the node embeddings, enabling variable-radius neighborhood expansions.

modules.name: Feature Lifting Module
modules.description: Aggregates node-level feature vectors to compute initial feature representations for the newly accepted higher-order cells and hyperedges using permutation-invariant operations like scaled sum projection.

modules.name: Topological Domain Constructor
modules.description: Assembles the accepted cells, edges, and vertices into valid topological domain objects (hypergraphs, simplicial complexes, or cell complexes), ensuring structural constraints such as simplicial closure are strictly maintained.

modules.name: Topological Neural Network Backbones
modules.description: Integrates and wraps downstream Topological Neural Network architectures (e.g., CWN, CXN, CIN, UniGCNII, UniGIN) to perform message passing and feature aggregation over the constructed lifted domains.

modules.name: End-to-End Training Pipeline
modules.description: Orchestrates the complete forward and backward passes linking the node embedding generator, differentiable lifting, feature projection, and TNN, while managing gradient flow through the STE, optimization steps, and early stopping protocols.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Module
modules.description: Computes all downstream task metrics used in the paper, including classification accuracy, Area Under the Curve (AUC), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for regression tasks.

modules.name: Static Lifting Baselines
modules.description: Implements the unsupervised, non-learnable graph lifting algorithms used for comparison, including cycle lifting, k-hop lifting, k-nearest neighbor lifting, and kernel-based lifting.

modules.name: Experiment Runner and Result Aggregator
modules.description: Manages the execution of multiple experimental runs across different datasets, TNN backbones, and lifting configurations, while aggregating statistics, computing standard deviations, and generating performance comparison tables.
